legs.name: estate-guard
legs.cmd: [ -n "${ABLATIVE_ESTATE_ROOT:-}" ] || { printf "REFUSED rc3: estate-guard requires ABLATIVE_ESTATE_ROOT, declared in this leg .environment. It is unset at this venue, so the estate claim census is UNMEASURED here — report it as a named declared omission, never a pass.\n" >&2; exit 3; }; sh "$ABLATIVE_ESTATE_ROOT/tools/gates/hooks/check_must_be_claimed.sh" "$ABLATIVE_ESTATE_ROOT"
legs.environment_reason: This leg asserts an ESTATE property, so it needs the estate root — which is not derivable from this repository. It was previously two hardcoded absolute Mac paths, which made the leg pass only on one machine and fail opaquely everywhere else. Declaring the requirement makes an off-estate venue REFUSE with rc 3 naming the missing declaration, so the run routes to a NAMED DECLARED OMISSION rather than a silent skip or a false green. A repo-relative path was rejected: it would make the stack/<repo> directory layout silently load-bearing and breaks in every worktree and off-box clone, which are exactly the venues batteries run in. Runner substitution of a declared root token is the better long-term design and waits for deliberate gates.py work.
legs.note: ESTATE ASSERTION, NOT THIS REPOSITORY'S. A red here names a SUBJECT repository and the seat who ruled its obligation, and that subject is usually not this repo -- this battery is only the clock. Take it to the named seat; do not delete this leg because it inconvenienced your landing. It asserts two things per listed row: that the repository carries refs/guards/shared-tree (the promise) and that the class-A guard is installed there as ruled (the mechanism). The population comes from docs/tracking/must-be-claimed.tsv, never from this repo. The trailing root runs the REVERSE arm (claimed but unlisted) -- without it, claim-without-listing then unclaim is a complete bypass of the witness, and it costs ~38s.
